resources.string: How arrival is detected, exit tracking
Working days, entry windows, holidays and leave
Live check of location and Wi-Fi
Add the places where your arrival should be logged. Up to three, for example your main office and a second site.
You can save up to %1$d workplaces.
Its location and Wi-Fi networks are removed. Days already logged are kept.
No places found. Try a different search or drop the pin on the map.
Search isn’t available right now (no connection or no geocoder on this phone). Drop the pin on the map instead.
200 m suits most offices. Smaller than 150 m causes false arrivals and exits.
Tap the map or drag the pin onto your office entrance.
Couldn’t get your location. Check that Location is on and try again outdoors or near a window.
Precise location is needed to place the pin. You can still search or tap the map.
Map not available in this build
No Google Maps API key was configured. Use “Use my current location” at the office, or enter coordinates.
Pick the Wi-Fi networks at your office. Connecting to one is usually the fastest and most battery-friendly arrival signal.
Location permission needed to see Wi-Fi names
Android only reveals Wi-Fi network names to apps with precise location permission. ArriveLog uses them only to recognise your office.
No networks visible. At the office, connect to the office Wi-Fi or tap Scan. You can also type the name below.
Stricter: only the access points seen when you ticked the network count. Re-tick at the office if the access points change.
Count as present when in range
Arrival can also be detected when the network is visible but not connected. Only checked when the phone is already awake, so it costs no extra battery.
Android limits how often apps may scan. If the list is empty, wait a moment and tap Scan again.
Recommended. Either signal logs the arrival, whichever comes first.
Stricter. You must be inside the geofence and on office Wi-Fi.
Office Wi-Fi only. The geofence is still used to detect when you leave.
Location only. Use when the office has no usable Wi-Fi.
Records the time you leave, ignoring short trips under 10 minutes.
Remind me to add the exit time
Two hours after expected end, if no exit was detected.
Uses more battery. The logged time is equally accurate either way; this only makes the notification come sooner.
Detection only runs during each day’s entry window. Days set to Off get no detection and no notifications.
Set at least one working day.
None. Add public holidays or leave so no arrival is expected on those days.
Days that use this profile will be set to Off.
Arrivals are only detected in this window (and up to 15 minutes before it).
Used for “On time / Late” and to know when to stop watching for your exit.
The entry window must end after it starts (same day).
Expected end must be after expected start.
Expected start is outside the entry window, so an on-time arrival wouldn’t be detected.
ArriveLog works offline. Location and Wi-Fi names never leave this phone.
Needed to place your office on the map, to read Wi-Fi network names, and for geofencing.

ArriveLog collects location data to detect when you arrive at and leave your workplace, even when the app is closed or not in use. This is only active during your entry window on working days. Location data stays on this phone and is never shared or uploaded.
On the next screen choose “Allow all the time”.
Turn on Location. For reliable geofencing also keep Google Location Accuracy on (Settings → Location → Location services).
To confirm arrivals (“Arrived 08:07 — logged”) and to remind you if no arrival was detected.
Lets ArriveLog see nearby Wi-Fi networks, used to recognise your office network.
Samsung delays or blocks background events for restricted apps, which can make arrivals late or missed. ArriveLog is designed to use under 1% battery a day even when unrestricted.

On Samsung: Settings → Apps → ArriveLog → Battery → Unrestricted. Then Settings → Device care (Battery and device care) → Battery → Background usage limits: make sure ArriveLog is not in “Sleeping apps” or “Deep sleeping apps”, and add it to “Never sleeping apps”.
In the list, select All apps → ArriveLog → Don’t optimise. Or open the app’s battery settings and choose Unrestricted.
If Android no longer shows the prompt, enable it in settings.
Arrival detection can’t work until location is allowed all the time and Location is on. You can finish setup and come back from Settings.
Inside %1$s (%2$d m from centre, radius %3$d m)
Connected, but the network name is hidden (location permission or Location off).
Office network name, but a different access point (strict matching is on).
If the entry window were open now, your arrival would be logged.
If the entry window were open now, no arrival would be logged.
Today is not a working day.
Background detection is on once setup is finished. Notifications arrive in the next update; until then check Settings → Debug log.
This detection mode needs at least one office Wi-Fi network.
No working days in the schedule.
Location not allowed all the time.
Battery optimised: Samsung may delay detection.
Every detection signal, accepted or ignored, with the reason
